seen_animation: A rhino-like doodle (large oval body on the left, a smaller teardrop head on the right, a zigzag of three horn points, short stub legs, a small tail stroke at the left end) stands facing right in front of a grey fence line and a grey vertical post. In frames 1-2 the head is held fairly upright with the horn zigzag pointing straight right, roughly level with the middle of the body. Between frames 2 and 3 the head swings down in one step so the horns point down and to the right toward the ground. From frame 3 to frame 16 the head stays lowered with the horn tips near the ground line, wobbling slightly. In frames 9-12 the whole figure sits further left, with the tail end cut off at the left edge, and in frames 13-16 it returns to roughly its earlier position. The legs barely change; the rear legs shrink to single short strokes in frames 9-12.
seen_film: A rhinoceros seen in side view, facing right, stands in a sandy enclosure in front of a fence. Through the whole shot it holds its head down with its snout on or near the ground at the lower right, rooting or grazing; in frames 1-4 dust or dirt is visible around its snout and the head is already low. From frame 5 onward the head is low and slightly nodding, the horn tip near the ground, while the tail swings. The body stays broadside; the camera framing drifts so the rhino sits further left (rump cropped at the left edge) in frames 9-12 and returns somewhat right in frames 13-16. There is no raising of the head anywhere in the 16 frames.
named_subject: a rhinoceros (the doodle's oval-body, teardrop-head, zigzag-horn rhino, mirrored to face right)
evidence: Frames 1-2: the animation's head is raised and the horns point horizontally right, while film frames 1-2 already show the rhino's head down at the ground with dust at its snout. Frame 2 to frame 3: the animated head rotates down by a large angle in a single step, which reads as a pop; the film has no such head drop. Frames 3-16: the animation holds the lowered head with horn tips near the ground, which matches film frames 3-16 well. Frames 9-12: the figure shifts left with the tail cropped, matching the film's framing drift in frames 9-12. Frames 9-12: the rear legs shrink to a single short stroke each, while the film's legs stay full. Still frames only; playback was not seen.
primary_gap: The animation opens with the head raised and then drops it abruptly between frames 2 and 3, whereas the film shows the head already lowered and rooting at the ground from frame 1.
closes_when: Frames 1 and 2 show the head already tilted down with the horn tips near the ground line, matching the pose of frames 3-4, so no large head rotation occurs between frames 2 and 3.
protect: The doodle's construction (two overlapping ovals for body and head, the three-point horn zigzag, short paired stub legs, the doubled tail stroke) drawn in the same thin black single-line style; the right-facing orientation matching the film; the lowered-head rooting pose held through frames 3-16 with small wobble; the leftward framing drift in frames 9-12 and return in 13-16.
identity_gap: The character is the doodle mirrored to face right with its ovals, horn zigzag and stub legs intact; the only drift is the rear legs shrinking to single short strokes in frames 9-12.
